question.prompt:
If this path is to continue in the same pattern, then which sequence of arrows goes from point \(425\) to point \(427?\)

[Figure 1](figures/1994_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Starting at point \(0\), the directions repeat as
\[
\text{right, up, right, down}.
\]
Each complete block uses four moves, so after a complete block the same sequence of directions starts again. Since
\[
425=4\cdot106+1,
\]
reaching point \(425\) takes \(106\) complete blocks followed by the first move of the next block, which goes right. The next two moves are therefore the second and third moves of that block: up from \(425\) to \(426\), then right from \(426\) to \(427\).

The required sequence is \(\boxed{\text{up, then right}}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Locate the point within a repeating block
